title: AUGUR: Proactive Failure Anticipation for Reliable Large Language Model Reasoning
content: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities, yet their autoregressive reasoning process remains vulnerable to early errors that can propagate throughout long reasoning trajectories. Existing approaches mainly rely on external exploration or post-hoc reflection, correcting mistakes only after they have occurred. In this work, we introduce AUGUR, a pre-mortem reasoning framework that enables LLMs to proactively anticipate potential failures before executing detailed reasoning. AUGUR consists of two key components. First, Pre-mortem Structured Cold-Start (PM-CS) constructs failure-aware supervision by contrasting successful and unsuccessful reasoning trajectories, enabling the model to identify likely failure points and corresponding verification strategies. Second, Risk-Guided Reinforcement Learning (RG-RL) extends GRPO with explicit rewards for failure anticipation and effective verification, jointly optimizing answer correctness and reasoning reliability. Extensive experiments across multiple model architectures and mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that AUGUR consistently outperforms strong RL-based baselines, improving average accuracy over GRPO by 5.01, 4.28, and 5.66 percentage points on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Qwen3-4B-Base, respectively. These results demonstrate that proactively modeling potential failures provides an effective paradigm for improving robust and reliable LLM reasoning.
